State Distribution Plot Over Time

Source: R/distribution_plot.R
distribution_plot.Rd

distribution_plot() draws how the states are distributed at each time point: for every position column it counts the sequences in each state and stacks the shares (or counts) as areas (default) or bars. It takes the same inputs as sequence_plot() (wide sequences, networks built from sequences, clusterings, mixture fits and tna models), draws one panel per group or cluster, and is the figure sequence_plot(type = "distribution") draws.

The plot shows the composition of the sample at each time point, not how individual sequences move: the same bands can come from sequences that stay in one state or from sequences that change state at every step. Look at single sequences with sequence_plot() and at the transitions with build_tna(). Missing cells form their own band by default (na), so sequences that end early stay visible instead of inflating the other shares.

Usage

distribution_plot(
  x,
  group = NULL,
  scale = c("proportion", "count"),
  geom = c("area", "bar"),
  na = TRUE,
  trim = NULL,
  trim_clusterwise = FALSE,
  state_colors = NULL,
  na_color = "grey90",
  frame = FALSE,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  main = NULL,
  show_n = TRUE,
  time_label = "Time",
  xlab = NULL,
  y_label = NULL,
  ylab = NULL,
  tick = NULL,
  ncol = NULL,
  nrow = NULL,
  combined = TRUE,
  legend = c("right", "bottom", "none"),
  legend_size = NULL,
  legend_title = NULL,
  legend_ncol = NULL,
  legend_border = NA,
  legend_bty = "n",
  cols = NULL
)

Arguments

x

The sequences: a wide data frame or matrix (one row per sequence, one column per time point), a netobject built from sequences, a netobject_group, a net_clustering, a net_mmm or a tna model. A clustering, a mixture fit or a netobject_group gives one panel per cluster or group. A one-hot or association network, and a frame or matrix holding only 0 and 1 (unless cols declares a frame's columns as positions), raise an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

group

A vector of one group label per sequence (length nrow(x)), drawing one panel per group in the order of its factor levels (sorted for a character or numeric vector). NULL (default) uses the cluster assignments carried by a net_clustering, net_mmm or netobject_group; a group given overrides them. Grouped panels are titled "Cluster <label>", whatever the grouping.

scale

What the y-axis shows: "proportion" (default) divides each time point by its total, so the bands fill 0 to 1; "count" keeps the counts, and the axis reaches the tallest stack.

geom

How the bands are drawn: "area" (default) as stacked polygons, "bar" as stacked bars.

na

Whether missing cells are drawn as an extra band coloured na_color. Default TRUE. With FALSE they are left out, and the proportions are shares of the observed states at each time point.

trim

Cuts the time axis (one number) or the time axis and the rows (two numbers); NA on either leaves that axis alone. Default NULL (no cut). The first number: a fraction in (0, 1) keeps the busiest time points that together hold that share of the observed states, wherever they sit, and the kept ones close up under their own labels (trim = 0.95); a value of 1 or more keeps the first that many time points (trim = 50). The second number ends each sequence earlier before the proportions are taken: a count keeps its first that many observed states, a fraction its first share of them (trim = c(0.9, 0.9)); no sequence is removed.

trim_clusterwise

For grouped plots with a fractional trim: FALSE (default) chooses one set of time points over all sequences, so every panel has the same time axis; TRUE chooses them within each group, so panels can differ in width.

state_colors

Colours for the state bands: an unnamed vector, one colour per state in sorted state order, or a named vector such as c(plan = "#0072B2"), where only the named states change and the rest keep the Okabe-Ito defaults. Names this plot does not draw are dropped with a message, so one palette can serve several figures. NULL (default) uses the palette stored on x with set_state_colors(), or the Okabe-Ito palette.

na_color

The colour of the missing-cell band. Default "grey90".

frame

Whether to draw a box around each panel, and axis lines. Default FALSE.

width, height

Size of a new graphics device, in inches, opened only in an interactive session (the other dimension defaults to 7). Default NULL (draw on the current device).

main

The plot title. With several panels on one figure it is drawn above them; with several panels and combined = FALSE it is not drawn. Default NULL.

show_n

Whether to add the number of sequences, "(n = N)", to the title of each panel. Default TRUE.

time_label

The x-axis label. Default "Time"; NULL or "" draws none.

xlab

Another name for time_label; when given, it wins.

y_label

The y-axis label. Default NULL: "Proportion" or "Count", following scale.

ylab

Another name for y_label; when given, it wins.

tick

Label every tick-th time point. Default NULL, which thins the labels to at most about 15.

ncol, nrow

The panel grid. Default NULL: with neither given, ncol = ceiling(sqrt(G)) and nrow = ceiling(G / ncol) for G panels; with one given, the other follows. With combined = FALSE the grid does not affect the layout, but ncol * nrow must still be at least the number of panels or an error is raised.

combined

Whether to draw all panels on one figure. TRUE (default) arranges them with graphics::layout(); FALSE draws each panel on its own page with its own legend, for knitr (fig.show = "asis") or for saving each panel to its own file. A single panel ignores it.

legend

Where the legend goes: "right" (default), "bottom" or "none".

legend_size

The legend text size. Default NULL, which scales it with the device width, between 0.65 and 1.2.

legend_title

A title for the legend. Default NULL (none).

legend_ncol

The number of legend columns. Default NULL: one column on the right, one row at the bottom.

legend_border

The colour of the swatch borders. Default NA (none).

legend_bty

The legend box: "n" (default) draws none, "o" draws one.

cols

For a wide data frame: the columns holding the time points. Needed when they are not a numbered run (T1, T2, ...), when one of them is called action, or when any other column sits beside them. Given for any other input, it raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input. Default NULL.

Value

Invisibly, a list describing the drawn figure:

counts

A named list, one entry per panel, each a state by time point matrix of counts; rows are named by levels, columns are the time points kept.

proportions

The same matrices with each column divided by its total (an empty time point stays 0).

levels

The state labels in plotting order, with "NA" appended when na = TRUE.

palette

The fill colours, one per entry of levels.

groups

The panel labels ("all" when ungrouped), in the order of counts and proportions.

See also

sequence_plot, build_clusters

Examples

distribution_plot(as.data.frame(trajectories))
